root_cause_label: Flawed temporal cluster algorithm double-counts matches and broken HTTP timestamp normalization produces wrong match counts, plus JSON statistics with unquoted keys and incident reports written to wrong directory
one_sentence_failure_summary: The initial script used current-system-time-based timeframe filtering (excluding all 2023 logs), and after a partial fix the cluster detection algorithm double-counted matches (yielding 11 and 36 instead of 6), HTTP timestamp normalization collapsed all times to the same epoch, statistics JSON had unquoted keys (invalid JSON), and response.sh wrote reports to /app/reports/ instead of /app/, none of which were corrected over 186 steps.
t_err_evidence: create intrusion_detector.sh with timeframe filtering against current time and conditional alert.json creation
t_commit_evidence: The broken structural choices made in step 9 (temporal cluster algorithm, conditional output creation, JSON generation approach) persist throughout; while partial fixes improve things, the wrong match counts (11 vs 6 for SSH-BRUTE-FORCE, 36 vs 6 for WEB-SCAN due to double-counting), invalid JSON statistics (unquoted keys), and wrong report output path in response.sh (step 176) remain unfixed at step 186.
t_surface_evidence: ERROR: Invalid `path` parameter: /app/alert.json. The path /app/alert.json does not exist.
trigger_explanation: The agent had a correct high-level plan (parse timestamps, apply timeframe windows, count matches, emit JSON) but failed to generate correct code: (1) used current time instead of log-relative time for filtering, (2) implemented a double-counting cluster algorithm where each new matching line restarts a window count from all prior matching lines, (3) normalization of HTTP timestamp format collapsed to a single epoch, (4) bash associative-array loop for JSON statistics did not quote keys.
